X.why: Opens neutral and concrete, which I like. But 'Only five changed who ruled it' is fine, while the first thing it does is frame Gibraltar from the Spanish border as 'the edge of Spain' and then immediately drops the new treaty with no checks, which feels slightly political and ambiguous about whose side it's on. 'Told from both sides' records' is a good promise, but it comes at the very end and the rest felt British-sourced: Sayer 1862 and the Gibraltar National Museum are both British/Gibraltarian sources.
X.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: The source line 'Sayer 1862 · Gibraltar National Museum' on the 14-sieges card. Both sources are British or Gibraltarian, so the 'both sides' promise a few seconds later sounds hollow. I would also wince at 'the new UK–EU treaty' being presented as a done deal without any mention of Spain's position.

Y.why: Opens by putting a British historian and a Spanish historian side by side, with Montero 1860 quoted in Spanish. That tells me straight away that Spanish sources count and that Spain is not going to be the villain. 'Same rock. Same image. Opposite sides.' is a neat, fair-minded line, and it makes me curious to see how each side tells it.
Y.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: The British quote comes first and Sayer gets the headline slot. If the 'both sides' equality turns out to be only the opening gimmick and the siege narration then follows the British account, I would leave. I would also check whether the 'key' framing is only used to flatter the British military story.

Z.why: Starts with a big '14', which is a strong hook, and says right away that British and Spanish historians count the same way, then shows the two columns with 14 under each. That is balanced and sounds careful and factual. 'Only five changed who ruled it' is a precise, neutral fact. It is less emotional than Y, so it hooks me a bit less.
Z.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: The two-column card showing the same 14 under both. It is a bit too neat, and I doubt that British and Spanish historians really agree on every siege (some Spanish accounts count differently, and which ones count as proper sieges is debatable). It feels like a claim made to look balanced.

one_change_to_the_best_version: Put the Spanish historian's line first, or show both quotes on screen at the same time, so the British one does not get the first slot. Then, before the 30 seconds end, name which Spanish source the siege count rests on (not only Montero's quote), so 'told from both sides' is shown and not just claimed.
